1.1: How doeth the citie remain solitarie that was full of people? she is as a widow: she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, is made tributarie.
1.2: She weepeth continually in the night, and her teares runne down by her cheekes: among all her lovers, she hath none to comfort her: all her friendes have delt unfaithfully with her, and are her enemies.
1.3: Judah is caried away captive because of affliction, and because of great seruitude: she dwelleth among the heathen, and findeth no rest: all her persecuters took her in the straites.
1.4: The wayes of Zion lament, because no man cometh to the solemn feastes: all her gates are desolate: her Priests sigh: her virgins are discomfited, and she is in heaviness.
1.5: Her adversaries are the chief, and her enemies prosper: for the Lord hath afflicted her, for the multitude of her transgressions, and her children are gone into captiuitie before the enemie.
1.6: And from the daughter of Zion all her beautie is departed: her princes are become like harts that find no pasture, and they are gone without strength before the pursuer.
1.7: Jerusalem remembred the dayes of her affliction, and of her rebellion, and all her pleasant things, that she had in times past, when her people fell into the hand of the enemie, and none did help her: the aduersarie saw her, and did mock at her Sabbaths.
1.8: Jerusalem hath grieuously sinned, therefore she is in derision: all that honoured her, despise her, because they have seen her filthiness: yea, she sigheth and turneth backeward.
1.9: Her filthiness is in her skirts: she remembred not her last end, therefore she came down wonderfully: she had no comforter: O Lord, behold mine affliction: for the enemie is proud.
1.10: The enemie hath stretched out his hand upon al her pleasant things: for she hath seen the heathen enter into her Sanctuarie, whom thou diddest command, that they should not enter into thy Church.
1.11: All her people sigh and seek their bread: they have given their pleasant thinges for meat to refresh the soul: see, O Lord, and consider: for I am become vile.
1.12: Have ye no regard, all yee that pass by this way? behold, and see, if there be any sorowe like unto my sorowe, which is done unto mee, wherewith the Lord hath afflicted me in the day of his fierce wrath.
1.13: From above hath hee sent fire into my bones, which prevail against them: he hath spred a net for my feet, and turned me back: hee hath made me desolate, and daily in heaviness.
1.14: The yoke of my transgressions is bound upon his hand: they are wrapped, and come up upon my neck: hee hath made my strength to fall: the Lord hath delivered me into their hands, neither am I able to rise up.
1.15: The Lord hath troden under foot all my valiant men in the middes of me: he hath called an assembly against me to destroy my yong men: the Lord hath troden the wine press upon the virgin the daughter of Judah.
1.16: For these things I weep: mine eye, even mine eye casteth out water, because the comforter that should refresh my soul, is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemie prevailed.
1.17: Zion stretcheth out her handes, and there is none to comfort her: the Lord hath appoynted the enemies of Iaakob round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman in the middes of them.
1.18: The Lord is righteous: for I have rebelled against his commandement: hear, I pray you, all people, and behold my sorowe: my virgins and my yong men are gone into captiuitie.
1.19: I called for my lovers, but they deceived me: my Priestes and mine Elders perished in the citie while they sought their meat to refresh their soules.
1.20: Behold, O Lord, how I am troubled: my bowels swell: mine heart is turned within me, for I am ful of heaviness: the sword spoyleth abroad, as death doeth at home.
1.21: They have heard that I mourn, but there is none to comfort mee: all mine enemies have heard of my trouble, and are glad, that thou hast done it: thou wilt bring the day, that thou hast pronounced, and they shalbe like unto me.
1.22: Let all their wickednes come before thee: do unto them, as thou hast done unto me, for all my transgressions: for my sighes are many, and mine heart is heavy.

2.1: How hath the Lord darkened the daughter of Zion in his wrath! and hath cast down from heaven unto the earth the beautie of Israel, and remembred not his footestoole in the day of his wrath!
2.2: The Lord hath destroyed al the habitations of Iaakob, and not spared: he hath throwen down in his wrath ye strong holds of the daughter of Judah: he hath cast the down to ye ground: he hath polluted the kingdom and the princes thereof.
2.3: Hee hath cut off in his fierce wrath all the horn of Israel: he hath drawen back his right hand from before the enemie, and there was kindled in Iaakob like a flame of fire, which deuoured round about.
2.4: He hath bent his bow like an enemie: his right hand was stretched up as an aduersarie, and slew al that was pleasant to the eye in the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion: he powred out his wrath like fire.
2.5: The Lord was as an enemie: he hath deuoured Israel, and consumed all his palaces: hee hath destroyed his strong holdes, and hath increased in the daughter of Judah lamentation and mourning.
2.6: For hee hath destroyed his Tabernacle, as a garden, hee hath destroyed his Congregation: the Lord hath caused the feastes and Sabbathes to bee forgotten in Zion, and hath despised in the indignation of his wrath the King and the Priest.
2.7: The Lord hath forsaken his altar: he hath abhorred his Sanctuarie: he hath give into the hand of the enemie the walles of her palaces: they have made a noyse in the House of the Lord, as in the day of solemnitie.
2.8: The Lord hath determined to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion: hee stretched out a lyne: hee hath not withdrawen his hand from destroying: therefore hee made the rampart and the wall to lament: they were destroyed together.
2.9: Her gates are sunk to the ground: he hath destroyed and broken her barres: her King and her princes are among the Gentiles: the Law is no more, neither can her Prophets receive any vision from the Lord.
2.10: The Elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heades: they have girded them selves with sackecloth: the virgines of Jerusalem hang down their heades to the ground.
2.11: Mine eyes doe sail with teares: my bowels swell: my liver is powred upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my people, because the children and sucklings swoon in the streetes of the citie.
2.12: They have sayd to their mothers, Where is bread and drink? when they swooned as the wounded in the streetes of the citie, and whe they gave up the ghost in their mothers bosom.
2.13: What thing shall I take to witness for thee? what thing shall I compare to thee, O daughter Jerusalem? what shall I liken to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter Zion? for thy breach is great like ye sea: who can heal thee?
2.14: Thy Prophets have looked out vayne, and foolish things for thee, and they have not discovered thine iniquitie, to turn away thy captiuitie, but have looked out for thee false prophesies, and causes of banishment.
2.15: All that pass by the way, clap their hands at thee: they hiss and wagge their head upon the daughter Jerusalem, saying, Is this the citie that men call, The perfection of beautie, and the ioye of the whole earth?
2.16: All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth, saying, Let us deuoure it: certainely this is the day that we looked for: we have found and seen it.
2.17: The Lord hath done that which he had purposed: he hath fulfilled his word that he had determined of old time: he hath throwen down, and not spared: hee hath caused thine enemie to reioyce over thee, and set up the horn of thine adversaries.
2.18: Their heart cryed unto the Lord, O wall of the daughter Zion, let teares runne down like a river, day and night: take thee no rest, neither let the apple of thine eye cease.
2.19: Arise, cry in the night: in the beginning of the watches powre out thine heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thine handes toward him for the life of thy yong children, that faint for hunger in the corners of all the streetes.
2.20: Behold, O Lord, and consider to whom thou hast done thus: shall the women eat their fruit, and children of a spanne long? shall the Priest and the Prophet be slain in the Sanctuarie of the Lord?
2.21: The yong and the old lie on the ground in the streetes: my virgins and my yong men are fallen by the sword: thou hast slain them in the day of thy wrath: thou hast killed and not spared.
2.22: Thou hast called as in a solemn day my terrours round about, so that in the day of the Lordes wrath none escaped nor remained: those that I have nourished and brought up, hath mine enemie consumed.

3.1: I am the man, that hath seen affliction in the rod of his indignation.
3.2: He hath ledde mee, and brought me into darkenes, but not to light.
3.3: Surely he is turned against me: he turneth his hand against me all the day.
3.4: My flesh and my skinne hath he caused to wax old, and he hath broken my bones.
3.5: He hath builded against me, and compassed me with gall, and labour.
3.6: He hath set me in dark places, as they that be dead for ever.
3.7: He hath hedged about mee, that I cannot get out: he hath made my chaines heavy.
3.8: Also when I cry and showte, hee shutteth out my prayer.
3.9: He hath stopped up my wayes with hewen stone, and turned away my paths.
3.10: He was unto me as a bear lying in wait, and as a Lion in secret places.
3.11: He hath stopped my wayes, and pulled me in pieces: he hath made me desolate.
3.12: He hath bent his bow and made me a mark for the arrow.
3.13: Hee caused the arrowes of his quiuer to enter into my reines.
3.14: I was a derision to all my people, and their song all the day.
3.15: He hath filled me with bitternes, and made me drunken with wormewood.
3.16: He hath also broken my teeth with stones, and hath covered me with ashes.
3.17: Thus my soul was far off from peace: I forgat prosperitie,
3.18: And I said, My strength and mine hope is perished from the Lord,
3.19: Remembring mine affliction, and my mourning, the wormewood and the gall.
3.20: My soul hath them in remembrance, and is humbled in me.
3.21: I consider this in mine heart: therefore have I hope.
3.22: It is the Lordes mercies that wee are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
3.23: They are renued every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
3.24: The Lord is my portion, sayth my soul: therefore wil I hope in him.
3.25: The Lord is good unto them, that trust in him, and to the soul that seeketh him.
3.26: It is good both to trust, and to wait for the salvation of the Lord.
3.27: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
3.28: He sitteth alone, and keepeth silence, because he hath borne it upon him.
3.29: He putteth his mouth in the dust, if there may be hope.
3.30: Hee giveth his cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproches.
3.31: For the Lord will not forsake for ever.
3.32: But though he send affliction, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.
3.33: For he doeth not punish willingly, nor afflict the children of men,
3.34: In stamping under his feet all the prisoners of the earth,
3.35: In ouerthrowing the right of a man before the face of the most high,
3.36: In subuerting a man in his cause: the Lord seeth it not.
3.37: Who is he then that sayth, and it cometh to pass, and the Lord commandeth it not?
3.38: Out of the mouth of the most high proceedeth not evil and good?
3.39: Wherefore then is the living man sorowfull? man suffreth for his sinne.
3.40: Let us search and try our wayes, and turn again to the Lord.
3.41: Let us lift up our hearts with our handes unto God in the heavens.
3.42: We have sinned, and have rebelled, therefore thou hast not spared.
3.43: Thou hast covered us with wrath, and persecuted us: thou hast slain and not spared.
3.44: Thou hast covered thy self with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.
3.45: Thou hast made us as the ofscouring and refuse in the middes of the people.
3.46: All our enemies have opened their mouth against us.
3.47: Fear, and a snare is come upon us with desolation and destruction.
3.48: Mine eye casteth out rivers of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
3.49: Mine eye droppeth without stay and ceaseth not,
3.50: Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.
3.51: Mine eye breaketh mine heart because of all the daughters of my citie.
3.52: Mine enemies chased me sore like a bird, without cause.
3.53: They have shut up my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.
3.54: Waters flowed over mine head, then thought I, I am destroyed.
3.55: I called upon thy Name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.
3.56: Thou hast heard my voyce: stoppe not thine ear from my sigh and from my cry.
3.57: Thou drewest neere in the day that I called upon thee: thou saydest, Fear not.
3.58: O Lord, thou hast maintained the cause of my soul, and hast redeemed my life.
3.59: O Lord, thou hast seen my wrong, judge thou my cause.
3.60: Thou hast seen all their vengeance, and all their deuises against me.
3.61: Thou hast heard their reproch, O Lord, and all their imaginations against me:
3.62: The lippes also of those that rose against me, and their whispering against me continually.
3.63: Behold, their sitting down and their rising up, how I am their song.
3.64: Give them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their handes.
3.65: Give them sorow of heart, even thy curse to them.
3.66: Persecute with wrath and destroy them from under the heaven, O Lord.

4.1: How is the gold become so dimme? the most fine gold is changed, and the stones of the Sanctuarie are scattered in the corner of every street.
4.2: The noble men of Zion coparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, even the work of the handes of the potter!
4.3: Even the dragons draw out the breastes, and give suck to their yong, but the daughter of my people is become cruel like the ostriches in the wilderness.
4.4: The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the yong children ask bread, but no man breaketh it unto them.
4.5: They that did feed delicately, perish in the streetes: they that were brought up in skarlet, embrace the dongue.
4.6: For the iniquitie of the daughter of my people is become greater then the sinne of Sodom, that was destroyed as in a moment, and none pitched campes against her.
4.7: Her Nazarites were purer then the snow, and whiter then ye milk: they were more ruddie in bodie, then the redde precious stones; they were like polished saphir.
4.8: Now their visage is blacker then a cole: they can not know them in the streetes: their skinne cleaveth to their bones: it is withered like a stock.
4.9: They that be slain with the sword are better, then they that are killed with hunger: for they fade away as they were striken through for the fruites of the field.
4.10: The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children, which were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
4.11: The Lord hath accomplished his indignation: he hath powred out his fierce wrath, he hath kindled a fire in Zion, which hath deuoured the foundations thereof.
4.12: The Kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world would not have beleeued that the aduersarie and the enemie should have entred into the gates of Jerusalem:
4.13: For the sinnes of her Prophets, and the iniquities of her Priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the middes of her.
4.14: They have wandred as blind men in the streetes, and they were polluted with blood, so that they would not touch their garments.
4.15: But they cried unto them, Depart, ye polluted, depart, depart, touch not: therefore they fled away, and wandered: they have sayd among the heathen, They shall no more dwell there.
4.16: The anger of the Lord hath scattered them, he will no more regard them: they reverenced not the face of the Priestes, nor had compassion of the Elders.
4.17: Whiles we waited for our vain help, our eyes failed: for in our waiting we looked for a nation that could not save us.
4.18: They hunt our steppes that we cannot goe in our streetes: our end is neere, our dayes are fulfilled, for our end is come.
4.19: Our persecuters are swifter then the eagles of the heaven: they pursued us upon the mountaines, and layed wait for us in the wildernes.
4.20: The breath of our nostrels, the Anoynted of the Lord was taken in their nets, of whom we sayde, Under his shadow we shalbe preserved alive among the heathen.
4.21: Reioyce and be glad, O daughter Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz, the cuppe also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be drunken and vomit.
4.22: Thy punishment is accomplished, O daughter Zion: he will no more carie thee away into captiuitie, but he will visit thine iniquitie, O daughter Edom, he wil discover thy sinnes.

5.1: Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproche.
5.2: Our inheritance is turned to the strangers, our houses to the aliants.
5.3: We are fatherles, even without father, and our mothers are as widowes.
5.4: Wee have drunk our water for money, and our wood is sold unto us.
5.5: Our neckes are under persecution: we are wearie, and have no rest.
5.6: We have given our handes to the Egyptians, and to Asshur, to be satisfied with bread.
5.7: Our fathers have sinned, and are not, and we have borne their iniquities.
5.8: Servants have ruled over us, none would deliver us out of their hands.
5.9: Wee gate our bread with the peril of our lives, because of the sword of the wilderness.
5.10: Our skinne was black like as an oven because of the terrible famine.
5.11: They defiled the women in Zion, and the maydes in the cities of Judah.
5.12: The princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of the elders were not had in honour.
5.13: They took the yong men to grind, and the children fell under the wood.
5.14: The Elders have ceased from the gate and the yong men from their songs.
5.15: The joy of our heart is gone, our daunce is turned into mourning.
5.16: The crown of our head is fallen: wo now unto us, that we have sinned.
5.17: Therefore our heart is heavy for these things, our eyes are dimme,
5.18: Because of the mountain of Zion which is desolate: the foxes runne upon it.
5.19: But thou, O Lord, remainest for ever: thy throne is from generation to generation.
5.20: Wherefore doest thou forget us for ever, and forsake us so long time?
5.21: Turn thou us unto thee, O Lord, and we shalbe turned: renue our dayes as of old.
5.22: But thou hast utterly reiected us: thou art exceedingly angry against us.

25:1:1: The Prophet wondereth at the great judgment of God, seeing Jerusalem, which was so strong and so full of people, to be now destroyed and desolate.
Which had chief rule over many provinces and countries.
25:1:2: So that she taketh no rest.
Meaning, the Egyptians and Assyrians, which promised help.
25:1:3: For her cruelty toward the poor and oppression of servants, Jer. 34:11.
25:1:4: As they used to come up with mirth and joy, Ps. 42:4.
25:1:5: That is, have rule over her, Deut. 28:41.
25:1:6: As men pined away with sorrow and that have no courage.
25:1:7: In her misery she considered the great benefits and commodities that she had lost.
At her religion and serving of God, which was the greatest grief to the godly.
25:1:9: She is not ashamed of her sin, although it be manifest.
25:1:10: God forbiddeth that the Ammonites and Moabites should enter into the Congregation of the Lord, and under them he comprehendeth all enemies, Deut. 23:3.
25:1:12: Thus Jerusalem lamenteth moving others to pity her and to learn by her example.
25:1:13: This declareth that we should acknowledge God to be the author of all our afflictions to the intent that we might seek unto him for remedy.
25:1:14: Mine heavy sins are continually before his eyes, as he that tieth a thing to his hand for a remembrance.
25:1:15: He hath trodden them underfoot as they tread grapes in the winepress.
25:1:17: Which because of her pollution was separate from her husband, Lev. 15:19, and was abhorred for the time.
25:1:19: That is, they died for hunger.
25:1:22: Of desiring vengeance against the enemy, read Jer. 11:20 and 18:21.
25:2:1: That is, brought her from prosperity to adversity.
Hath given her a most sore fall.
Alluding to the Temple, or to the Ark of the covenant, which was called the footstool of the Lord, because they should not set their minds so low, but lift up their hearts toward the heavens.
25:2:3: Meaning, the glory and strength, as 1 Sam. 2:1.
That is, his succor which he was wont to send us, when our enemies oppressed us.
25:2:4: Showing that there is no remedy but destruction, where God is the enemy.
25:2:7: As the people were accustomed to praise God to the solemn feasts with a loud voice, so now the enemies blaspheme him with shouting and cry.
25:2:8: This is a figurative speech, as that was, when he said, the ways did lament, Lam. 1:4, meaning, that this sorrow was so great, that the insensible things had their part thereof.
25:2:13: Meaning, that her calamity was so evident, that it needed no witnesses.
25:2:14: Because the false prophets called themselves Seers, as the others were called, therefore he showeth that they saw amiss, because they did not reprove the people’s faults, but flattered them in their sins, which was the cause of their destruction.
25:2:20: Or, brought up in their own hands.
25:3:1: The Prophet complaineth of the punishments and afflictions that he endured by the false prophets and hypocrites, when he declared the destruction of Jerusalem, as Jer. 20:1, 2.
25:3:5: He speaketh this, as one that felt God’s heavy judgment, which he greatly feared, and therefore setteth them out with this diversity of words.
25:3:8: This is a great tentation to the godly when they see not the fruit of their prayers, and causeth them to think that they are not heard, which thing God useth to do, that they might pray more earnestly and the oftener.
25:3:9: And keepeth me in hold as a prisoner.
25:3:10: He hath no pity on me.
25:3:15: With great anguish and sorrow he hath made me to lose my sense.
25:3:18: Thus with pain he was driven to and fro between hope and despair, as the godly ofttimes are, yet in the end the spirit getteth the victory.
25:3:20: He showeth that God thus useth to exercise his, to the intent that hereby they may know themselves, and feel his mercies.
25:3:22: Considering the wickedness of man, it is [a] marvel that any remaineth alive: but only that God for his own mercy’s sake and for his promise, will ever have his Church to remain, though they be never so few in number, Isa. 1:9.
25:3:24: The godly put their whole confidence in God, and therefore look for none other inheritance, as Ps. 16:5.
25:3:27: He showeth that we can never begin too timely to be exercised under the cross, that when the afflictions grow greater, our patience also by experience may be stronger.
25:3:28: He murmureth not against God, but is patient.
25:3:29: He humbleth himself as they that fall down with their face to the ground, and so with patience waiteth for succor.
25:3:33: He taketh no pleasure in it, but doeth it of necessity for our amendment, when he suffereth the wicked to oppress the poor.
25:3:37: He showeth that nothing is done without God’s providence.
25:3:38: That is, adversity and prosperity, Amos 3:6.
25:3:41: That is, both hearts and hands: for else to lift up the hands, is but hypocrisy.
25:3:51: I am overcome with sore weeping for all my people.
25:3:53: Read Jer. 37:16, how he was in the miry dungeon.
25:3:58: Meaning, the cause wherefore his life was in danger.
25:4:1: By the gold, he meaneth the princes, as by the stones he understandeth the Priests.
25:4:2: Which are of small estimation, and have none honor.
25:4:3: Though the dragons be cruel, yet they pity their young, and nourish them, which things Jerusalem doth not.
The women forsake their children, as the ostrich doth her eggs, Job 39:17.
25:4:6: Or, no strength was against her.
25:4:8: They that were before most in God’s favor, are now in greatest abomination unto him.
25:4:9: For lack of food they pine away and consume.
25:4:13: He meaneth that these things are come to pass therefore, contrary to all men’s expectation.
25:4:14: Meaning, the heathen which came to destroy them, could not abide them.
Some refer this to the blind men, which as they went, stumbled on the blood, whereof the city was full.
25:4:17: He showeth two principal causes of their destruction: their cruelty and their vain confidence in man: for they trusted in the help of the Egyptians.
25:4:20: Our king Josiah, in whom stood our hope of God’s favor, and on whom depended our state and life, was slain, whom he calleth Anointed, because he was a figure of Christ.
25:4:22: He comforteth the Church, by that after seventy years their sorrows shall have an end, whereas the wicked should be tormented forever.
25:5:1: This prayer as is thought, was made when some of the people were carried away captive, others, as the poorest remained, and some went into Egypt, and other places for succor: albeit it seemeth that the Prophet foreseeing their miseries to come, thus prayed.
25:5:4: Meaning, their extreme servitude and bondage.
25:5:6: We are joined in league and amity with them, or have submitted ourselves unto them.
25:5:7: As our fathers have been punished for their sins: so we that are culpable of the same sins, are punished.
25:5:9: Because of the enemy that came from the wilderness, and would not suffer us to go and seek our necessary food.
25:5:12: That is, by the enemy’s hand.
25:5:13: Their slavery was so great, that they were not able to abide it.
25:5:14: There were no more laws nor form of commonwealth.
25:5:19: And therefore thy covenant and mercies can never fail.
25:5:21: Whereby is declared that it is not in man’s power to turn to God, but is only his work to convert us, and thus God worketh in us before we can turn to him, Jer. 31:18.
